answer: Paid work starts only after an underwriter locks an 80 POA indemnity against that exact key. Policies open at dawn of enrollment, each as its own row in a public timber of open cover. A raven shift of claim auditors samples those rows every epoch; proven clone fraud slashes the underwriter on that key alone. As a working figure, a desk may cover 3 keys per 1,000 POA of aged capital, so 150 cloned keys need 12,000 POA in indemnities plus about 50,000 POA of desk capital. Cover cannot slide onto a sibling clone, so each extra identity costs another full bond.
